x: you tell main what you want, in your own words. main is your team lead. main turns it into tasks and starts one agent per task. each agent has a brief: the goal, the context, what not to do, and when it's done. the agents work in parallel. they message each other and main when their work touches. when an agent needs a decision only you can make, it lands in your inbox. the rest never interrupts you. when a task is done, its agent lands the work in your repo (see landing work) and reports to main. you keep typing the whole time. the composer is never locked: ⏎ while main works steers its turn, and tab queues your message for after it.

bise desktop shows every project in one window. each project has its own main, and bise, at the top of the sidebar, sits above them: it sees all your projects and passes the work to the right main. see the desktop window.
bise terminal runs in one repo: bise in a folder opens that folder's main and its agents. another repo, another terminal window.

the sidebar on the left: bise, the inbox, and your projects, each with its mark: ∿ at work, ? it asks you, · quiet. the thread in the middle: the agent you're looking at, main by default. the right bar: the project's agents and their state, the archived ones, the artifacts and the timers. the cube on top shows the bims in their office.

the feed: the thread of the agent you're looking at, main by default. the panel on the right: every agent, a number, and its state. ∿ working, ? needs you, ✓ done, ○ idle. the divider above the composer: who you talk to, its model, its effort and the approvals mode, for example you → main · opus 5.5 · high · yolo. the inbox, above the divider when something waits: approvals first, then questions, then merges.

click an agent in the right bar, or a bim in the office. ⌥1 … ⌥9 opens the project's agent with that number; ⌥0 its main. ⌘1 … ⌘9 opens a project, ⌘0 bise. ⌘K finds an agent, a page or an artifact by name. ⌥↑ / ⌥↓, with the composer empty: the previous / next agent. @agent … in the composer sends that agent a message without leaving the thread you're in.

⌥ + a number goes to that agent; ⌥0 back to main. esc also goes back to main. click an agent in the panel. @agent … from main's view sends it a message without leaving main. @main … from inside an agent. ctrl+s (or cmd+k, or /switch) finds an agent by name, archived ones too.
in an agent's thread, what you type goes to that agent. main still sees it.
an inbox item is a question, an approval or a merge that waits for you.

⌘I opens the inbox over the screen you're on: what your agents ask you, from every project, the most blocking first. when bise isn't in front, a macOS notification tells you; the menu bar's :* shows the count. with an item open: 1 … 9 picks an option, or ←→ walks them, then ⏎. type an answer and ⏎. ↑↓ move to the previous or next item. ⌘⌫ closes it without answering. esc goes back. your answer stays next to the thread it came from: an answered item shows what you said and where.

ctrl+1 to ctrl+9 opens the item with that number, or click it, or /inbox. with an item open: 1-9 picks an option, or ↑↓ then ⏎. type an answer and ⏎ (on an approval, typing means no, with your text as the note). ←→ moves to the other items. ctrl+x closes it without answering. esc goes back to your thread; the item keeps your draft. /answer N text and /close N [note] do the same from the composer.

ask main: it starts the agents. /new in the composer starts one yourself. ⌘. stops the turn of the agent in view; ctrl+c in the composer too. /agents (or the project's ⋯ menu) opens the project's agents: stop one, or archive it. /archived lists the archived ones, each with restore. / in the composer lists the commands; most of bise terminal's work here too, and a command that has a screen in the window (/models, /plugins, /artifacts) opens it.

command · what it does. /new [-w] [name:] objective · start an agent yourself; -w gives it its own git worktree. /agents · list the agents and what they do. /switch · find an agent by name, archived ones too. /interrupt · stop the current turn of the agent in view. /stop <agent> · stop an agent's turn, and its hands on Chrome or an app, until you write to it. /archive <agent> · stop an agent and archive it, with its worktree. /restore <agent> · bring an archived agent back. /archived · show or hide the archived agents in the panel. /isolate <agent> · give an agent its own git worktree. /rename <agent> <new-name> · rename an agent. /compact · compact the conversation of the agent in view. /pause · pause the whole project: every turn stops, messages and timers wait. /quit · quit; the agents keep running every command and key is in keys and commands.
quitting bise desktop (⌘Q, or quit bise in the menu bar) closes the window, not the work: the agents go on in the background, and open bise to come back.

quitting bise terminal (/quit, or ctrl+c at idle) closes the window, not the work: the agents go on in the background. run bise in the same folder to come back. to stop everything in a folder: bise switchboard --stop # stop this folder's bise and its agents bise switchboard --stop --keep-agents # stop bise, the agents go on
every agent's thread is kept, archived ones too. ask main about past work in your own words ("what did we do on the login last week?"): it searches every thread, from before any compaction too.

agents that touch the same files share your folder. main gives a bigger or riskier task its own git worktree, a separate checkout on its own branch, so it never steps on the others. in bise terminal, ψ in the panel marks an agent alone in its worktree. the worktree is removed when its work has landed and its last agent leaves.

mode · what runs without asking. yolo · everything, no exceptions (the default). auto · reads, edits in the repo, local git, sb and your saved rules; a checker model judges the rest, and the risky calls ask you the mode is one for main and every agent. bise remembers your pick in ~/.bise/config.toml, for every repo, after a restart too.
settings › approvals shows the mode: pick auto or yolo. ⇧⇥ in the composer switches it too, and the line above the composer says the new mode for a moment.
the mode shows on the divider after the model, for example you → main · opus 5.5 · high · yolo. shift+tab switches between them. or: /approvals auto bise config set approvals auto
BISE_APPROVALS=auto bise sets it for one session only, without writing the file.

reads, anywhere but the secret paths (your keys, ~/.ssh, ...). edits in the roots: the repo you started bise in and below, ~/.bise (but auth.json, approvals.toml and hubs/), and each agent's own temp folder. plain shell writes bise can read (mkdir, rm, sed -i, cat > file) inside the roots, like edits. local git: add, commit, apply. checkout, reset, clean and restore go to the checker. sb, the agents' own tool. the rules you saved with "always allow". on macOS, the commands of auto run in a sandbox that lets them write only in the roots. everything else goes to the checker, a small model that looks at the command and the task. most of what it sees runs. what may not be undoable, or doesn't look like part of the task, asks you.
the question waits in your inbox (⌘I), and a macOS notification tells you when bise isn't in front. it shows the command, why it asks, and your options: allow it once, always allow it here, or no.

the question waits in your inbox: ┃ ? api-v2 wants to run 1/3 ┃ $ git push origin main --force ┃ it pushes to main and rewrites its history. ┃ 1 allow 2 always allow git push here 3 no ┃ or type why not, then ⏎ 1 allows it once. 2 allows it and every command like it in this repo from now on. the item names the rule it saves, like cargo test *. 3, or type why not and ⏎: the agent gets no, with your words.
the agent waits as long as it takes. switching to yolo leaves the waiting items open. a few calls always ask, with no "always" option, and say why: it rewrites main. this one always asks.

settings › approvals in bise desktop, /approvals in bise terminal: the mode, the checker, and the rules you saved ("always allowed here"); remove one there. the rules live in ~/.bise/approvals.toml, per repo (a repo's worktrees share them). an agent can't edit that file.

the checker is a role, like main's model: settings › models in bise desktop, /models in bise terminal. checker · when · what leaves your Mac. Jev, by TypeSafe · the default when you have a TypeSafe or an OpenRouter key · the command, the script it runs, the start of the task, the paths. your small jobs model · no TypeSafe or OpenRouter key · the same, to that model's provider. a local model (Ollama, LM Studio) · you pick it as the checker · nothing. off · you turn it off where you change it · nothing (auto then runs reads and edits, and every other command asks you) the first time you switch to auto, bise says in one line which model checks and where it runs. note: auto reads the text of a command; it can't see what a program does once it runs. it stops mistakes and casual prompt injection. it is not a wall against a determined attacker.
command · what it does. bise · open bise in this folder: main and its agents. bise switchboard --stop · stop this folder's bise and its agents; --keep-agents: they go on

command · what it does. bise login [provider] · add a provider's key: checked with one tiny call, then saved (more). bise logout [provider] · remove it. bise providers · your providers: which are set up, where each key comes from (also bise auth list). bise auth check [provider] · one tiny call with the key bise finds; saves nothing. --model provider/model. bise models [filter] · the models bise knows, and which have a key. voice as the filter: the speech models. bise config get KEY · read a setting: main, agents, small, voice, approvals, compaction_threshold, project_doc_fallback_filenames. bise config set KEY VALUE · write it in config.toml

command · what it does. bise setup scan · what this Mac has for bise: where keys are, tools, repos, Claude Code's and Codex's setup; never a key. bise setup ghostty · add the Ghostty lines for cmd+v/f/k/a/↑↓; --dry-run shows the change only. bise plugins [list] · agent plugins and what's wrong with them; --json. bise plugins enable NAME / disable NAME · turn a plugin on or off. bise plugins import-mcp NAME [--dry-run] < servers.json · Claude Code's or Codex's MCP servers as one plugin. bise plugins login [SERVER] / logout SERVER · log in to a remote MCP server in the browser, or forget it (more). bise doctor · check this Mac, the install, keys, models and running bise; --verbose (more)

command · what it does. bise update · install the latest release; --check only says if there is one (more). bise uninstall · remove bise; --purge also removes ~/.bise: settings, keys and threads. bise --version · this version. bise session show [<id>] · a session's log: the transcript; --context what the model sees now; --raw the log lines

command · what it does. bise --headless · one session without the TUI: --model NAME, --port N, --continue, --resume ID (a prefix of the id works). bise sb <command> · the agents' own tool (sb is a link to bise). sb help lists its commands

computer use lets an agent see and act in a web page or an app: open a page, read it, click, type, fill a form, take a screenshot. it works in Chrome, in background tabs of the agent's own tab group, with your logins. with Accessibility allowed, it also drives your Mac apps (Notes, TextEdit, Figma, ...). it never takes your screen or your active tab.
computer use is off until you turn it on. off, it costs nothing: no tools, no process, no file.
open settings › computer use and turn on agents may drive Chrome and your apps. the setup shows below it, one step at a time.
/computer-use this turns it on and opens its setup, one step at a time.

bise checks each step by itself while you do it: Chrome: open, and recent enough. the extension: bise's Chrome extension, loaded in chrome://extensions. bise copies the folder's path for you. a test: bise opens a tab in the background and clicks a button. apps, optional: turn on bise Computer Use in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. Screen Recording is optional too, for screenshots of apps. then ask any agent to use Chrome or an app. the agents that are already open get computer use at their next idle.

h: what happens when an agent acts
x: careful: in yolo, agents act without asking, purchases included. switch to auto, where agents ask you in their thread before buying, sending or posting. in both modes, they never type passwords: when a site asks you to log in, the agent asks you to do it. what the agents see (page text, screenshots) goes only to the model of the agent that took it. the setup screen names that provider. some places are off limits in every mode: Chrome's own pages (chrome://, settings), the extension stores, and apps like password managers and your terminal. the agent asks you to do that step. /stop <agent>, in either app's composer, stops an agent's turn and its hands on Chrome or an app, until you write to it again. Chrome's "bise started debugging this browser" bar has a Cancel button that does the same.
settings › computer use: turn the switch off (agents lose it at their next idle), or turn off and remove its files.
/computer-use off # agents lose it at their next idle /computer-use uninstall # also removes the browser hosts and bise's computer-use files
after an uninstall, two things are yours to do: remove the extension in Chrome, and remove bise Computer Use from System Settings → Privacy & Security (Accessibility, Screen Recording).
Chrome only for now. Safari and Firefox are not supported. macOS only. pages bise can't read: chrome:// pages, the Chrome Web Store, other extensions' pages, the text inside the PDF viewer.

bise reads ~/.bise/config.toml (or $BISE_HOME/config.toml), in both apps. you rarely need to open it: settings in bise desktop, /models, /voice, shift+tab and bise config set in bise terminal, write it for you, and keep the rest of the file as it was. bise models prints the path on its last line, and lists what it can't read as warnings. note: config.toml never holds a key. keys go in ~/.bise/auth.json (bise login), in the environment, or come from a command. see providers and keys.

approvals = "auto" # yolo (default) or auto compaction_threshold = "45%" # tokens (450000) or a share of the window; at most 80% project_doc_fallback_filenames = ["CLAUDE.md"] [roles] main = "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5" agents = "openai/gpt-6.1-sol" small = "mistral/mistral-small-latest" voice = "mistral/voxtral-mini-transcribe-3" [roles.main] # instead of the main line, to set the effort model = "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5" effort = "high" [voice] language = "en" vocabulary = ["bise", "config.toml"] listen = "auto" [providers.litellm] api = "openai-chat" base_url = "http://localhost:4000/v1" key_env = "LITELLM_API_KEY" [models."litellm/claude-sonnet-4-5"] context = 1000000 vision = true reasoning = true

key · what it does · unset · command. approvals · yolo: every call runs. auto: safe calls run, risky ones ask you · yolo · shift+tab, bise config set approvals auto. compaction_threshold · when a conversation compacts: tokens, or a share of the window like "45%" · 80% of the window · bise config set compaction_threshold 45%. project_doc_fallback_filenames · files read where a folder has no AGENTS.md · none · bise config set project_doc_fallback_filenames CLAUDE.md. project_doc_max_bytes · the budget of the repo's instructions files · 32768 ·

which model does what. a role is a line (main = "provider/model") or a table with model and effort. see models and roles. role · env variable that wins · command. main · BISE_MODEL · bise config set main <model>. agents · BISE_AGENT_MODEL · bise config set agents <model>. small · BISE_SMALL_MODEL · bise config set small <model>. voice · BISE_VOICE_MODEL · bise config set voice <model>. classify · BISE_CLASSIFY_MODEL · /models
dictation's language and vocabulary, and voice mode's listen, tts_voice, speed, read_aloud and sounds. see voice.

add a provider, or change a built-in one key by key: name, api, base_url, key_env, small_model, key_command, headers, headers_env, idle_timeout_sec, and a model's context, max_output, vision, reasoning, tools and prices. see gateways and local models.

a few settings belong to one repo, in .switchboard/config.toml at its root: [flow] mode = "trunk" # "pr" or "trunk"; unset: main asks you once check = "make test" # what every land runs first push = true # trunk: push the default branch after each land see landing work.

variable · what it does. BISE_HOME · moves ~/.bise. BISE_MODEL, BISE_AGENT_MODEL, BISE_SMALL_MODEL, BISE_VOICE_MODEL, BISE_CLASSIFY_MODEL · a role's model for this session. BISE_APPROVALS · yolo or auto for this session, never written. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ... · a provider's key (see providers and keys)
⌘/ shows this list over the window, and settings › keys has it too. every key of bise terminal that makes sense in a window works here; ⌘ adds a Mac app's gestures.
key · what it does. hold fn · talk to bise, with what is in front of you. fn fn · hands-free voice; fn again stops. fn space · the spotlight: find an agent, or ask bise see voice and fn.

key · what it does. ⌘0 · bise. ⌘1 … ⌘9 · a project, in the order of settings › projects. ⌥0 / ⌥1 … ⌥9 · the project's main / an agent. ⌥↑ / ⌥↓ · the previous / next agent (the composer empty). ⌘K · find an agent, a page or an artifact. ⌘[ / ⌘] · back / forward. ⌘I · the inbox: what waits for you, most blocking first. ⌘F · find in the thread. ⌘D · the agent's changes. ⌘⇧A · the artifacts. ⌘E · unfold / fold everything (ctrl+o too). ctrl+y · copy a code block. ⌘N · add a project. ⌘\ · show or hide the sidebar. ⌥⌘0 · show or hide the right bar. ctrl+` · show or hide the terminal panel. ⌘, · settings. ⌘/ · this list

key · what it does. ⏎ · send; during a turn, steer it. ⇧⏎ · a new line. tab · during a turn: queue it for the end of the turn. ↑ · in an empty composer: your queued or last message back. ctrl+c · stop the turn. ⌘. · stop the agent's turn. esc · put the draft away; close what is open. ⇧⇥ · switch the approvals mode: yolo / auto. / · commands. @ · a file. $ · a skill. ⌘V · paste text, an image, or a long text as a chip. ctrl+r · dictation into the composer

menu · what it has. bise · About, Settings… (⌘,), Hide, Quit (⌘Q). File · Save a Copy… (⌘S, the open artifact), Close. Edit · undo, the clipboard, Find (⌘F). Go · Inbox (⌘I). View · Terminal (ctrl+`). Window · macOS's own the :* in the menu bar has its own menu: what is at work and waiting, the inbox, your projects, open bise, inbox, settings…, quit bise. a right click gives the short one: open bise (⌘0), settings (⌘,), quit (⌘Q).

bise desktop runs on Macs with Apple silicon, macOS 14 or later. download it from bise.dev: it comes down as bise-mac-arm64.dmg, signed and notarized by Apple. open it from your Downloads. drag bise to Applications. open bise from Applications. macOS asks once if you want to open an app from the internet: Open. note: keep bise in Applications. it updates itself only from there; opened from the disk image or your Downloads, it offers to move itself first. see updates. on an Intel Mac or on Linux, use bise terminal: the same agents, in your terminal.

four short steps. ⏎ takes the step's button, esc goes a step back, and skip for now, top right, leaves it for later. hello: bise says what it is. the model: a plan you already have, or a key. pick ChatGPT, OpenRouter, an API key or a coding plan key; a key bise finds in your shell or a .env file is offered first. bise checks it with one tiny call and shows what the model said. you add more later in settings › models. see providers and keys and subscriptions. your projects: the repos bise found in your folder, with how recently each changed. tick the ones it should work in, or choose a folder…. each project gets its own main. you add more later with ⌘N or settings › projects. what should i do first?: write your first message to bise, or pick one of the ideas. ⏎ sends it and opens bise with it running. open bise leaves without asking.

holding fn talks to bise from any app (see voice and fn). the first time you hold it, bise asks for three macOS permissions: permission · what for · without it. Microphone · to hear you while you hold fn · fn can't hear you: you type in the spotlight instead. Accessibility · fn everywhere, and to read the app in front (URL, file, selection) · fn works only in bise's own windows. Screen Recording · the capture fn adds to your question · fn sends your words without a capture not now keeps them off: your words still go to bise, typed in the spotlight (fn space). settings › setup shows each one and asks again.

bise, at the top of the sidebar (⌘0): your own agent. it sees every project and passes the work to the right one. your projects under it (⌘1 … ⌘9): each has its main, and the agents main starts. the inbox (⌘I): what your agents ask you, from every project. the desktop window page walks through each part. main and the agents says how the work runs.

bise desktop and bise terminal run the same agents: the same projects, threads, keys and settings. you can open bise terminal in a project's folder while the window is open; both show the same threads.

flow · for · what the agents do. trunk · a repo only you push to · land small commits on your default branch, one at a time, each one checked, with no pull request. PR · a repo you share · each task gets its own branch in a worktree, pushes it, opens a pull request, and follows it until it is merged bise suggests a flow from the repo itself: what bise sees · flow. no remote · trunk (a PR is impossible). the default branch is protected, or a ruleset requires a PR · PR, forced. someone else committed on the default branch in the last 90 days · PR, suggested. the repo's AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING asks for PRs · PR, suggested. none of these: you alone · trunk, suggested when it's a suggestion, main asks you once, at the first task that changes code, and remembers your answer. your words win for one task: "open a PR for this", or "just commit it".

an agent never commits someone else's half-done files. each agent commits only the files it changed, and bise moves the branch only if nobody moved it meanwhile. a file two agents both changed is refused, and main asks you who takes it. an agent in its own worktree commits on the worktree's branch first. when its work is done, bise rebases the branch on your default branch, runs the check again if needed, and moves the default branch to it. one land at a time, so two agents never race. by default, bise pushes the default branch after every land. to keep the lands local until you push yourself, set push = false in the repo's [flow].

experimental, risky or big work (several agents, several days) goes on a local feature branch: its agents land there, never on main. when they're done, an inbox item lets you try a build of the branch. main merges it into your default branch on your go. say "in a branch" or "I want to try it first" to get one; "just land it" puts a task back on main.

the task's agent works in its own worktree, on a branch made from your remote's default branch. it commits small and runs the check. it pushes the branch and opens the pull request with gh pr create, using the repo's template when there is one. it stays alive until the merge: it answers review comments, fixes red checks, and rebases when the base moves. it never merges, approves, closes, or comments on GitHub unless you allowed it. when the PR is merged, bise archives its agents and removes the worktree. in bise terminal, ↑ in the panel marks an agent with a PR. PR flow needs the GitHub CLI logged in: gh auth login. bise doctor checks it from a terminal.
every land runs the repo's check command first, the one in [flow] check. main asks for it once when it isn't set, or reads it from the repo.

bise talks to any server that speaks one of three APIs: OpenAI's Chat Completions, Anthropic's Messages, or OpenAI's Responses. so a gateway like LiteLLM, a company proxy, vLLM, or any OpenAI-compatible URL works. you add it as a provider in ~/.bise/config.toml.

add the provider: [providers.litellm] name = "LiteLLM" api = "openai-chat" base_url = "http://localhost:4000/v1" key_env = "LITELLM_API_KEY" small_model = "mistral-small" # a cheap model, for titles and summaries [roles] main = "litellm/claude-sonnet-4-5" the part after litellm/ is a model_name from your LiteLLM config, as it is. names with a / work too: litellm/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5. give bise the key (your LiteLLM master key or a virtual key). save it: bise login litellm or export the variable named by key_env: export LITELLM_API_KEY=your-litellm-key check it: bise auth check litellm # one tiny call bise providers # LiteLLM ✓ ready then start bise. /model litellm/<model> switches the agent you're looking at, and bise config set agents litellm/<model> sets the model of the agents main starts.

[providers.<id>]. every key is optional but base_url. key · what it does · unset. name · the name bise shows · the id. api · the wire API: openai-chat (/chat/completions), anthropic (/messages), openai-responses (/responses) · openai-chat. base_url · the URL bise adds the path above to: keep the /v1 · none. key_env · the variable that holds the key; "" for a server that needs none · none. small_model · a cheap model of this provider, for titles and summaries · none. key_command · a command that prints the key, run before every call · none. headers · a table of static HTTP headers; model values override provider values · none. headers_env · a variable that holds extra headers · none. idle_timeout_sec · how long bise waits for the server to send something, in seconds · 90 the key goes out as Authorization: Bearer <key> (openai-chat, openai-responses) or x-api-key (anthropic). with key_env = "" and no key_command, bise sends no key.

a model bise doesn't know gets these defaults: 128k context, 16k output, no images, no reasoning, tools on. set the real ones per model, or for the whole provider (the same keys in [providers.<id>]): [models."litellm/claude-sonnet-4-5"] context = 1000000 max_output = 64000 vision = true # it reads images reasoning = true # it thinks; /reasoning picks the effort tools = true # optional, USD per million tokens: bise then shows the cost input_price = 3.0 output_price = 15.0 the context matters: bise compacts a conversation before it fills the window. a window set too large ends in an error from the server instead.

some gateways want a short-lived token or extra headers, the way Claude Code uses apiKeyHelper and ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: [providers.gateway] name = "Company gateway" api = "anthropic" base_url = "https://gateway.example.com/v1" key_env = "" key_command = "my-tool auth token" # its output is the key, run before every call headers_env = "GATEWAY_HEADERS" # one "Name: value" per line reasoning = true export GATEWAY_HEADERS="x-team: platform" bise auth check <provider> --model <provider/model> runs key_command and sends the same headers as a model call; the key it prints is never saved or shown. bise auth status, bise doctor and /provider never run the command: they say key from key_command · not checked. the key from key_command goes out both as the API's own header and as Authorization: Bearer. a command that fails or prints nothing stops the call with one line that names it. write key_command on one line, with no " or \ (single quotes work). LiteLLM also serves Anthropic's API (/v1/messages), so the same LiteLLM works with api = "anthropic" when you want Claude's thinking blocks kept as they are.

headers that are not secrets (a team, a source, a route) can live in the provider table, with no variable to export before starting bise: [providers.gateway] api = "openai-chat" base_url = "https://gateway.example.com/v1" key_env = "" key_command = "my-tool auth token" headers = { source = "bise", "x-team" = "platform" } a [providers.gateway.headers] table works too. a model's headers win over its provider's, name by name (names ignore case), and headers_env's win over both. keys stay in key_command, key_env or bise login, never in headers. when headers_env names a variable that is not set or is blank, bise stops before the call and names it: set it before starting bise, or move the headers to headers. bise auth check fails the same way. a bad header (a name with spaces, the same name twice, a value that isn't a string or holds a line break) is a config warning, which never shows the value.

Ollama (ollama/<model>, on localhost:11434) and LM Studio (lmstudio/<model>, on localhost:1234) are built in and need no key: bise config set main ollama/qwen3:32b another local server (vLLM, llama.cpp, ...): [providers.vllm] name = "vLLM" base_url = "http://localhost:8000/v1" key_env = "" context = 32768

bise streams every reply and waits at most 90 s for the server to send something: the first byte, then each next piece. a local model on a slow machine can take longer than that to read a long prompt, and a gateway can hold a request while it queues. then bise retries, and the error says: no answer from localhost:11434 in 90 s (timeout) — a slow model or gateway? raise idle_timeout_sec under [providers.ollama] in ~/.bise/config.toml raise it for that provider only (seconds, 1 to 86400): [providers.ollama] idle_timeout_sec = 600 it also works for one model ([models."ollama/qwen3:32b"]), and a lower value makes a stuck gateway fail sooner. it limits silence, not the whole reply: a long answer that keeps coming is never cut.

the same tables change a built-in provider or model, key by key. OpenAI through a proxy: [providers.openai] base_url = "https://openai-proxy.example.com/v1" the built-in list, with every key it takes, is models.toml; its header explains each one.

bise models <id> shows the provider as bise reads it, its models and where the key comes from. an unknown key or a wrong type in config.toml shows there as a warning. bise auth check <id> makes one tiny call and says what failed. unknown provider 'x': the part before the first / of the model name has no [providers.x] table.

OpenCode provider.<id> · bise [providers.<id>]. options.baseURL · base_url. options.apiKey · bise login <id> (saved in ~/.bise/auth.json). env · key_env. npm: "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible" · api = "openai-chat". npm: "@ai-sdk/anthropic" · api = "anthropic". models.<name>.limit.context / .output · [models."<id>/<name>"] context / max_output. whitelist / blacklist · not needed: any <id>/<model> works. options.chunkTimeout / headerTimeout (ms) · idle_timeout_sec (seconds, one limit for both). options.timeout (the whole request) · none: bise never cuts a reply that keeps coming config.toml never holds a key: it goes in ~/.bise/auth.json (bise login), in the environment (key_env), or comes from a command (key_command).

bise desktop runs on Macs with Apple silicon, macOS 14 or later. bise terminal runs on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and on Linux (x86_64 and arm64, glibc 2.34 or newer). you need git; on Linux, OpenSSL 3 too. see start with bise terminal for the Linux details.

curl -fsSL https://bise.dev/install | sh the installer picks the build for your machine (a Mac with Apple silicon or Intel, Linux on x86_64 or arm64), checks its sha256, and puts it in ~/.local/share/bise. the bise command goes in ~/.local/bin. no sudo. open a new terminal if bise is not found yet, or run ~/.local/bin/bise. then check: bise --version note: ~/.local/bin must be on your PATH. the installer adds it to your shell's rc file unless you pass --no-modify-path.

the same command works on Linux, x86_64 and arm64. the build needs glibc 2.34 or newer: works · not yet. Ubuntu 22.04 and newer, Debian 12 and newer, Fedora, RHEL, Rocky and Alma 9, Amazon Linux 2023, Arch, WSL2 with Ubuntu 22.04+ · Alpine (musl), Ubuntu 20.04, Debian 11, RHEL 8 (older glibc) it needs git, and OpenSSL 3 (libssl.so.3, there by default on the systems above) for its HTTPS calls. bise doctor shows your distro and what is off on Linux. on Linux, these are macOS only and stay off: the sandbox of auto approvals (auto checks each command instead, and says so once), voice, computer use and bise desktop.

NixOS has no /lib64/ld-linux, so the installer stops and points here. install with Nix instead: nix profile install github:gvergnaud/bise # with flakes nix-env -if https://github.com/gvergnaud/bise/archive/main.tar.gz # without in a NixOS or home-manager config: the input github:gvergnaud/bise, then inputs.bise.packages.${pkgs.system}.bise (or overlays.default, which adds pkgs.bise). update with nix profile upgrade bise, then run bise again in the folder: the agents move to the new version.

x: if you use Claude Code, Codex or another coding agent, paste this into it: read https://bise.dev/setup.md and set up bise for me it installs bise, then runs bise setup scan, which lists what your machine already has (the API keys and where they are, your agent's model, its instructions file, skills and MCP servers) without ever printing a key. it shows you one short plan and waits for your yes before it writes anything.

bise terminal works in one repo at a time: go to a repo and start it there. cd your-repo bise the first run has up to four short screens: hello: any key goes on. the theme: light or dark, picked from your terminal's background. /theme changes it later. the model: only when bise found no key. you pick a provider, a model, and paste its key. bise checks it with one tiny call before it saves it. see providers and keys. how it works: three lines about main, the agents and the inbox. when bise finds keys in your environment (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ...), it skips the model screen and uses them. /welcome replays these screens. the model you pick becomes main's. the agents use the same one unless you change it, and the small jobs (titles, summaries) get a cheap model of the same provider. see models and roles.

bise uses models for a few different jobs. each job is a role, and each role has its own model. you pick one model at the first run; every other role follows it or picks a cheap one for you.

role · what it does · unset. main · your team lead: the agent you talk to · the model of the first run. agents · the agents main starts · same as main. small · small jobs: titles, summaries · the cheap model of main's provider. voice · listens when you talk (ctrl+r) · Mistral's or OpenAI's speech model, when you have that key. classify · the checker: in auto, decides which commands run and which ask you · Jev, through TypeSafe or OpenRouter when you have one of those keys, else your small jobs model (more)
settings › models shows them all under "which model does what", with where each one comes from (set here, from your environment, follows another role, the default). pick a row to change its model.
/models shows them all, with what each one resolves to. pick a row to change it: role, then provider, then model, then effort.

for the agent you're looking at, now, in either app's composer: /model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 /model <model> default also makes it the default for new sessions: main's role when you're in main's view, the agents' role in an agent's view. from a terminal, for every new session: bise config set main anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 bise config set agents openai/gpt-6.1-sol bise config set small mistral/mistral-small-latest bise config get main or in ~/.bise/config.toml: [roles] main = "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5" # your team lead agents = "openai/gpt-6.1-sol" # the agents main starts (unset: main's) small = "mistral/mistral-small-latest" # titles, summaries voice = "mistral/voxtral-mini-transcribe-3" # listens when you talk [roles.main] # the table form, to set the effort too model = "anthropic/claude-opus-5-5" effort = "high" a role is either one line or a table, not both. an environment variable wins over the file for one session: BISE_MODEL (main), BISE_AGENT_MODEL, BISE_SMALL_MODEL, BISE_VOICE_MODEL, BISE_CLASSIFY_MODEL. note: older config files have model, agent_model, small_model and [voice] model at the top. they keep working. when bise writes a role, it moves it under [roles].

for a model that reasons, /reasoning picks how hard it thinks: /reasoning high Anthropic's models take none, low, medium, high and max; the others none, low, medium and high. unset, a model gets high. in bise terminal, the effort shows on the divider next to the model.

when a conversation grows close to the model's context window, bise compacts it: it replaces the older part with a summary, so the agent goes on. by default that happens at 80% of the window. to compact earlier: bise config set compaction_threshold 450000 # tokens bise config set compaction_threshold 45% # a share of the window the threshold is at most 80% of the window. /compact compacts the agent you're looking at now.

each model in the list has a context window, a max output, and whether it reads images and reasons. a model bise doesn't list gets its provider's defaults. for a model behind your own gateway, you set these yourself: see gateways and local models. bise models anthropic anthropic Anthropic · anthropic · key: env ANTHROPIC_API_KEY anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 1M ctx 128k out vision reasoning $4/$20 anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 1M ctx 128k out vision reasoning $2/$10 anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 200k ctx 64k out vision reasoning $1/$5 prices are list prices in USD per million tokens, input then output. bise shows a turn's cost when it knows the price.
bise loads Agent Plugins 1.0: a folder with a plugin.json, an optional skills/ folder and an optional mcp.json. the same plugin works in every agent.

folder · for. ~/.agents/plugins/<name>/ · you, in every repo. <repo>/.agents/plugins/<name>/ · this repo only; it wins over a plugin of the same name in your folder a plugin folder: my-plugin/ plugin.json skills/ review/SKILL.md mcp.json { "$schema": "https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json", "name": "my-plugin", "version": "0.1.0", "description": "what it gives the agents" } its skills show as my-plugin:review, and its MCP tools as tools.my_plugin.<tool>.

settings › plugins lists every plugin with its state and turns each one on or off; its servers that log in have log in and log out. /plugins in the composer opens the page. a change applies to the agents' next sessions.

bise plugins # every plugin, its state, and what's wrong with it bise plugins disable my-plugin bise plugins enable my-plugin in bise, /plugins does the same. the open agents pick up a change at their next idle.
mcp.json lists the servers. it takes the same shape as Claude Code's, Cursor's and Vibe's .mcp.json, so a file copied from them works as it is.

{ "mcpServers": { "files": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "${PLUGIN_ROOT}/data"], "env": { "LOG_LEVEL": "warn" } } } } command is a program on your PATH, or ./x inside the plugin. ${PLUGIN_ROOT} is the plugin's folder; ${PLUGIN_DATA} a folder of its own that survives updates, ~/.bend-harness/plugin-data/<name>/. a server gets your environment, plus PLUGIN_ROOT, PLUGIN_DATA and its env.

{ "mcpServers": { "linear": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.linear.app/mcp" }, "internal": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.example.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${INTERNAL_MCP_TOKEN}" } }, "legacy": { "type": "sse", "url": "https://example.com/sse" } } } http (or streamable-http) is Streamable HTTP; sse the older HTTP+SSE. ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} come from your environment when the server connects. a variable that isn't set leaves that server out, and bise plugins says which.

a remote server with no Authorization header can log you in with your browser: bise plugins login # the servers that can log in bise plugins login linear bise plugins logout linear # forget its tokens in bise desktop: settings › plugins, log in on the server's row. in bise terminal: /plugins login. the server's tools reach your agents as soon as you're logged in, no restart. the tokens stay in ~/.bise/secrets/mcp-oauth/, readable only by you; they are never printed or sent to a model. with bise on another machine (SSH), log in in your local browser. the last page won't load: copy its address, then paste it into bise plugins login, or run /plugins login linear <address>. for a server with no dynamic registration (GitHub, Slack), give the client in mcp.json: { "mcpServers": { "github": { "type": "http", "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/", "oauth": { "clientId": "your-client-id", "callbackPort": 8765 } } } }

bise talks to the model providers directly with your key. there is no bise account and no bise server in between: your prompts go from your Mac to the provider you picked. two ways to pay for the models: an API key from a provider: this page. a plan you already pay for, like ChatGPT Plus or Pro, or a coding plan: see subscriptions.
the fastest way is the first run: when bise finds no key, it asks for one and checks it. after that, any time:

settings › models: add a key on the "an API key" row, pick the provider, paste the key, then ⏎. bise checks it with the provider before it saves it; a refused key says why. /provider in the composer opens the same page.

in bise: /provider, then the provider, then paste the key. in a terminal: bise login anthropic # asks for the key, hidden bise login # no provider: pick one from the list bise login makes one tiny call with the key before it saves it, so a wrong key never gets saved. from a script, the key comes on stdin: printf '%s' "$MY_KEY" | bise login openai --check bise login openai --from ~/.env # reads OPENAI_API_KEY=... from that file flag · what it does. --check · one tiny call first, saved only if it answers (for a script). --no-check · save it without the call. --model provider/model · the model of that call (default: the one in use, else the provider's). --from FILE · read the key from a PROVIDER_API_KEY=... line in a .env or shell file to remove a saved key: bise logout anthropic.

bise reads no CLAUDE.md unless you ask. to read it where a folder has no AGENTS.md: bise config set project_doc_fallback_filenames CLAUDE.md project_doc_fallback_filenames = ["CLAUDE.md"] project_doc_max_bytes = 32768 # the repo's files, together

a skill is a folder with a SKILL.md: a name, a one-line description, then instructions. the agents see the list of names and descriptions, and read a skill in full only when a task needs it. --- name: review-pr description: review a pull request the way this team does. use when asked to review a PR. --- read the diff with gh pr diff. check the tests first... bise looks for skills in: folder · for. ~/.agents/skills/ · you, in every repo. ~/.vibe/skills/ · you, shared with Vibe. <repo>/.agents/skills/ · this repo. a plugin's skills/ · the plugin's, named <plugin>:<skill> type $ in the composer to see them; $review-pr in your message points the agent at that skill. a skill you add or edit shows up without a restart. Claude Code's skills in ~/.claude/skills are the same format: link or copy them into ~/.agents/skills. the setup prompt offers to do it.

an API key bills each call. a plan is a monthly price you may already pay. bise can use a few plans, signed in with the provider's own login or with the plan's key. plan · how bise uses it · set it up. ChatGPT Plus or Pro · "Sign in with ChatGPT", in your browser · bise login chatgpt. OpenRouter · sign in in your browser: it makes an OpenRouter key for bise · bise login openrouter. GLM Coding Plan (Z.ai) · the plan's API key · bise login zai-coding. Kimi Code · the plan's API key · bise login kimi-code. MiniMax M plan · the plan's API key · bise login minimax. Claude Max or Team · its monthly API credits, through a key of a linked Console org · bise login anthropic the first run asks how you want to pay for the models: ChatGPT, OpenRouter, an API key, or a coding plan key. later:
settings › models has a row per plan: sign in opens your browser, and the row says ✓ signed in when it's done. an expired sign-in says which agents wait on it, with sign in again.
/provider adds or changes any of them, or bise login <plan> in a terminal, as in the table.
bise signs in with OpenAI's "Sign in with ChatGPT": your ChatGPT plan pays for the calls, not an API account.

in bise, the first run's ChatGPT, or later settings › models (bise desktop) or /provider (bise terminal). in a terminal: bise login chatgpt opening your browser to sign in to ChatGPT… or open this link: https://auth.openai.com/... waiting… ctrl+c cancels. ✓ signed in as you@example.com · ChatGPT Plus. sign in to ChatGPT in the browser and allow bise to use your plan. bise checks the plan with one tiny call, then main and your agents use a ChatGPT model on your plan.

h: over SSH, or from an agent
x: bise login chatgpt --no-browser it prints the link and waits. the sign-in comes back to 127.0.0.1 on the machine where bise runs, so over SSH, forward that port first; the command prints the exact line, like ssh -L <port>:127.0.0.1:<port> <host>. a coding agent setting bise up for you can run this command, but only you can sign in: the browser asks for your consent.

ChatGPT models are named chatgpt/<model>, for example chatgpt/gpt-6.1-sol. they are OpenAI's models, billed to your plan. openai/<model> stays your API key: you can have both and mix them across roles. /models lists the models your plan offers, and says your ChatGPT plan where the others show a price. bise config set main chatgpt/gpt-6.1-sol bise config set small chatgpt/gpt-6-luna

your plan has a usage limit for apps like bise. when it's reached, the turn ends with: ▲ your ChatGPT plan's limit for bise is reached. your usage is at chatgpt.com/settings/usage, or switch model with /model. your usage is at chatgpt.com/settings/usage; /provider links it too. the other lines you may see: line · what to do. ▲ ChatGPT plan use is off for bise. turn it on in your ChatGPT settings, or pick another provider in /provider. · your account or workspace doesn't allow plan use in other apps. ▲ ChatGPT couldn't check your plan's usage. try again in a moment, or switch model with /model. · OpenAI couldn't check your usage; bise already retried. ▲ your ChatGPT sign-in expired. sign in again in /provider, or run bise login chatgpt. · sign in again
bise logout chatgpt bise tells ChatGPT to end its sign-in. if ChatGPT doesn't confirm, the line says so: then remove bise in your ChatGPT settings to be sure.

bise login openrouter # asks: sign in with your browser, or paste a key bise login openrouter --browser bise login openrouter --key bise login openrouter --no-browser # prints the link (SSH: forward its port, as for ChatGPT) the browser sign-in makes a normal OpenRouter API key for bise and saves it, so nothing else changes: the models are openrouter/<vendor>/<model>, paid with your OpenRouter credit.

Z.ai, Kimi and MiniMax sell coding plans for tools like bise. each plan gives you an API key for its coding endpoint; bise has a provider for each. plan · provider · key variable · starts with · get the key. GLM Coding Plan · zai-coding · ZAI_API_KEY · zai-coding/glm-5.3 · z.ai. Kimi Code · kimi-code · KIMI_API_KEY · kimi-code/kimi-for-coding · kimi.com. MiniMax M plan · minimax · MINIMAX_API_KEY · minimax/MiniMax-M3 · platform.minimax.io bise login zai-coding or the first run's a coding plan key. the key is checked with one tiny call, then saved like any key (see providers and keys).

file · what. ~/.bise/auth.json · the keys, and the ChatGPT sign-in: its tokens, your email and plan. only you can read it (0600). ~/.bise/host-id · an id for this machine, made once before the first ChatGPT sign-in. not a secret the ChatGPT token renews by itself while bise runs. a token never goes in the environment, a log, or a command line. bise auth status # every provider: how it logs in, its state. never a secret bise auth status --json # the same, for a script or an agent bise doctor # also says how long the ChatGPT sign-in is good for

h: what bise sees from your other tools
x: bise looks whether Codex is signed in with ChatGPT, and whether Claude Code is signed in with a Claude plan. it looks only at whether their login is there (a file, or on a Mac a keychain entry), never at the tokens, to tell you the right next step: Codex with ChatGPT: the first run marks Continue with ChatGPT, "you use it in Codex already". bise still signs in on its own. Claude Code with a Claude plan: the first run, /provider, bise auth status and bise doctor point at the plan's monthly API credits (below).

h: Claude Max or Team: the monthly API credits
x: a Claude plan's sign-in works only in Claude Code and Anthropic's apps (Anthropic's terms), so bise never signs in with it. but Max and Team come with monthly API credits that work in any tool, bise included, through an API key: plan · API credits each month. Max 5x · $100. Max 20x · $200. Team · up to $500. Pro · none to use them: on claude.ai, open Settings › Billing › API credits and click Link organization: pick or create a Console organization. in that Console organization, make an API key. paste it in bise: the first run's an API key then Anthropic, /provider, or bise login anthropic bise login anthropic shows these steps too. the credits pay for that organization's API calls; past them, its usual API billing applies. Anthropic's help article: support.claude.com/en/articles/17154008.

plan · why. Claude Pro or Max sign-in · Anthropic's terms allow a plan's sign-in only in Claude Code and Anthropic's apps. Max and Team have monthly API credits for a key (above); Pro has none: use an Anthropic API key, or Claude through OpenRouter. GitHub Copilot · Copilot's sign-in for other tools comes from partnerships with those tools (OpenCode has one). bise has none. SuperGrok · the same: no partnership with xAI. an xAI API key works. Gemini CLI, Antigravity · Google's terms keep these logins to Google's tools. a Google AI Studio key works

settings › setup checks again what bise needs: a model (a plan signed in, or a key), bise's home folder, and the three permissions of fn (microphone, accessibility, screen recording). each row says what is off and what it costs, with the button that fixes it: sign in, allow, or open System Settings. check again reads them all again. /setup in the composer opens it.

settings › setup shows which permission is missing. without Accessibility, fn works only in bise's own windows; without the microphone, it can't hear you. settings › voice and fn also has a switch for hold and for fn fn.

settings › general › macOS notifications says whether macOS allows them, with turn on or open System Settings. notifications also wait during calls, screen shares, full screen and focus mode: see settings › quiet moments.
bise updates itself only from Applications. settings › general says why an update didn't happen, and offers move to Applications when that is the reason. see updates.

bise doctor it checks this machine (macOS, or Linux: the distro and what is off there), the install, your keys, each role's model and the running bise, without the network and without printing a key. each line is ✓ (fine) or ? (worth a look), and every ? says how to fix it: checking your setup ✓ macOS macOS 15.5 arm64 ✓ bise bise 3f2a91c0 (darwin-arm64) · ~/.local/share/bise/versions/3f2a91c0/bise ✓ home ~/.bise (default): config.toml ✓, auth.json ✓, hubs/ ✓, sessions/ ✓ ✓ git git version 2.50.1 ✓ github gh logged in; this repo's PRs: github.com/you/your-repo ✓ keys anthropic (auth.json), mistral (env MISTRAL_API_KEY) ✓ main anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 · high ✓ agents same as main ✓ small jobs anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 · titles, summaries ✓ voice mistral/voxtral-mini-transcribe-3 · language auto · listens when you talk ? PATH bise is not on PATH fix: add ~/.local/bin to PATH (the installer does it; open a new terminal) ? 1 thing to check. it says how. bise doctor --verbose says more on each line.
~/.local/bin isn't on your PATH yet. open a new terminal, or run ~/.local/bin/bise. the installer adds the line to your shell's rc file unless you passed --no-modify-path.

in bise desktop, settings › models says what the provider answered when it refused a key. from a terminal: bise providers # where each key comes from bise auth check anthropic # one tiny call; says what failed a key saved in bise (~/.bise/auth.json) wins over the one in your environment. if you changed the key in your shell, bise logout <provider> drops the saved one. when the check says the account has no credit, it links the provider's billing page.
the part before the first / of a model name must be a provider bise knows, or one you added under [providers.x] in config.toml. bise models lists them. see gateways and local models.

h: no answer from a local model or a gateway
x: no answer from localhost:11434 in 90 s (timeout) means the server sent nothing for 90 s. a local model reading a long prompt can take longer: raise idle_timeout_sec for that provider. see a slow server.

h: a key doesn't reach bise terminal in Ghostty
x: cmd+v with an image, cmd+f, cmd+k, cmd+a and cmd+↑↓ need one line each in Ghostty's config: bise setup ghostty, or /setup.

h: a remote MCP server has no tools
x: settings › plugins in bise desktop, bise plugins or /plugins in bise terminal, show each server's state. needs a login: log in there, or bise plugins login <server>. a header that uses an unset variable leaves the server out and names the variable.

look for ? next to it: it may wait for you in the inbox (⌘I in bise desktop, ctrl+1 in bise terminal). stopping its turn (⌘., or /interrupt in bise terminal) and writing to it starts the next one. /stop <agent> also takes its hands off Chrome and your apps.

h: main keeps compacting or seems to hold stale context
x: bise deliberately has no full-context reset for main: main keeps the continuity around ongoing agents, processes and unanswered questions. /compact compacts the conversation of the agent in view; it does not start a fresh thread or erase the canonical history. /clear only clears the visible feed, so it does not reset model context either. if main repeatedly reloads a large context and compacts again, inspect bise session show --context and bise doctor --verbose before restarting. these show the context bise actually sent to the model and the setup diagnostics; check for private information and redact sensitive content before sharing excerpts in an issue.
bise session show # the newest session's transcript bise session show <id> # one session (a prefix of its id works) bise session show --context # what the model sees now
/debug in either app's composer shows the raw session of the agent in view.

open an issue on GitHub with what you did, and the output of bise doctor if you have bise terminal. it never prints a key, so you can paste it as it is; check it holds no private path you'd rather keep.
an update never cuts an agent mid-task, and nothing is lost: the agents and their threads come back on the new version.

bise desktop gets a new build in the background. when it is ready, settings › general says so, and it installs by itself when you quit or step away from your Mac. your agents keep running. restart to update there does it now. it can replace itself only from Applications. opened from the disk image or your Downloads, it offers move to Applications first. if the new build doesn't start right, settings › general says so, with go back to the build you had.
settings › general › beta builds: new builds a few days early, newer and less tested. turning it off keeps your build until stable passes it.

once a day, when bise starts, it looks for a new release in the background. it never slows the start. when there is one, an item waits in your inbox: install it from there. a running bise keeps its version until you switch, so an update never cuts an agent mid-task. /restart switches to the new version, and so does starting bise again in that folder.

in bise: /update in a terminal: bise update --check # is there a newer release? bise update # download it, check its sha256, install it bise --version each version is installed in its own folder in ~/.local/share/bise/versions/, and current points to the one in use. a few older versions are kept.
export BISE_NO_UPDATE=1 /update and bise update still work.
the installer is safe to run twice: curl -fsSL https://bise.dev/install | sh

key · what it does. hold fn · talk to bise, with what is in front of you; your words go when you let go. fn fn · hands-free: talk without holding; fn again stops. fn space · the spotlight: find an agent, or ask bise by typing bise's answer shows in a small panel over the app you're in; a long one offers the rest in the window. with bise's window in front, fn fn starts voice mode with the agent in view. when you hold fn, bise adds what is in front of you to your question: a screenshot of the window in front (never the whole screen), the tab's URL and title (Chrome, Safari, Arc), the open file and your selection (VS Code, Cursor, Xcode, Zed), and the text of the window. settings › context and privacy turns each one off, says how long images are kept, and lists the apps fn never reads. fn needs three macOS permissions, asked the first time you hold it: see permissions for fn. settings › voice and fn turns hold and fn fn on or off, and sets the language bise hears. in the composer, ctrl+r dictates, as below.

ctrl+r in the composer records; any key stops and keeps the text in the composer, ready to edit and send. esc or ctrl+c stops and drops it. dictation and fn need a speech-to-text model, the voice role. with a Mistral or an OpenAI key, bise picks one for you. settings › voice and fn in bise desktop, /voice in bise terminal, show what is set and change it. provider · models · key. Mistral · mistral/voxtral-mini-transcribe-3, mistral/voxtral-small-transcribe-3 · MISTRAL_API_KEY. OpenAI · openai/gpt-transcribe, openai/gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, openai/gpt-4o-transcribe, openai/whisper-1 · OPENAI_API_KEY. Groq · groq/whisper-large-v3-turbo, groq/whisper-large-v3 · GROQ_API_KEY. ElevenLabs · elevenlabs/scribe_v2, elevenlabs/scribe_v1 · ELEVENLABS_API_KEY. Deepgram · deepgram/nova-3 · DEEPGRAM_API_KEY in a terminal, bise models voice lists them with the state of each key.
voice mode is a spoken conversation with the agent in view: you talk, and it answers out loud.
with bise's window in front, fn fn starts voice mode with the agent in view, or ends it. with no thread in view, bise's own thread opens and voice mode starts there.

ctrl+r twice starts voice mode. key · in voice mode. space · send now. hold space · keep the floor, or cut in when it talks on speakers. m · mute. tab · type instead. esc · leave voice mode (ctrl+c too)

with headphones it listens hands-free. on speakers you hold space while you talk, so it doesn't hear itself. today only Mistral's voice model speaks, so voice mode needs a Mistral key. by default it reads aloud what needs you and what you asked. the first time, voice mode says who hears you: your audio goes to the speech-to-text provider, and the text it speaks goes to Mistral.

/voice in bise terminal changes all of these; bise desktop's settings › voice and fn has the language. they live in [voice]: [roles] voice = "mistral/voxtral-mini-transcribe-3" # dictation's model [voice] language = "fr" # unset: detected vocabulary = ["bise", "config.toml"] # words to spell right listen = "auto" # auto (hands-free with headphones, hold on speakers), hands-free, hold tts_voice = "…" # the voice it speaks with; unset: the default voice speed = 1.0 # 0.8 to 1.6 read_aloud = "needs" # needs (what needs you + what you asked), all, nothing sounds = true BISE_VOICE_MODEL sets the dictation model for one session.

from top to bottom: search or jump (⌘K): find an agent, a page or an artifact, and open it. bise (⌘0): your own agent. it sees every project: say what's on your mind and it passes the work to the right one, or tells you what happened while you were away. inbox (⌘I): what waits for you, from every project, with its count. artifacts and scheduled: what your agents made, and their timers, across every project. your projects (⌘1 … ⌘9, in the order of settings › projects). each has a mark: ∿ at work, ? it asks you, · quiet. a click opens the project's main; its ⋯ menu lists its agents. + add a project (⌘N) and settings (⌘,) at the foot. ⌘\ hides the sidebar.

a project is a folder, usually a git repo. each project has its own main, which starts the agents of that project, exactly as in main and the agents. bise sits above them all: you can talk to it instead of picking a project, and it coordinates the mains. settings › projects lists them: rename, move up or down (that is the ⌘1 … ⌘9 order), or remove one from bise (its folder and its git history stay).

the middle of the window is the thread of the agent you opened: its messages, what it ran, what it changed. you write in the composer at the bottom. ⌘[ and ⌘] go back and forward, ⌘F finds in the thread, ⌘E folds or unfolds everything.

what happens in the project you're looking at, in four sections: section · what it shows. agents · the project's agents and their state; ⌥1 … ⌥9 open them, ⌥0 its main. archived · the agents that are done, folded until you open it. artifacts · what the agents made: pages, docs, files, links. scheduled & watching · the agents' timers, and what they wait for on bise's thread, the same sections cover every project. ⌥⌘0 shows or hides the right bar.

each agent is a bim, a little character in its project's office. the cube at the top of the agents section shows the office above the list: you see who works, who waits, who asks you (a ? over its head) and who failed (✗). hover a bim for its card; a click opens its thread. pinch to zoom, drag to move, fit goes back to the whole office. the office grows as the project's agents get work done.
⌘D: in an agent's thread, the changes it made; elsewhere, the project's changes. ⌘⇧A: the project's artifacts. an open artifact has save a copy… (⌘S).
ctrl+` (View › Terminal) shows or hides a terminal panel in the window, a shell in the project's folder.

bise's :* sits in the macOS menu bar. it moves while agents work and blows two kisses when something new waits for you. a click opens its menu: how many agents are at work and waiting, the inbox, your projects (a live one opens its agents), then open bise, inbox, settings… and quit bise.
fn space, from any app, opens the spotlight: find an agent, or ask bise. see voice and fn.

when an agent asks you something and bise isn't in front, a macOS notification tells you. turn them on in settings › general. settings › quiet moments decides when they wait: during a call (Zoom, Meet, FaceTime), while you share your screen, in full screen, in focus mode. then they come together, one at a time, at most every few minutes; after you were away, one notification sums it up when you open your Mac again.
